encoding.notes: Predicate is a bare truthiness test on the dict value kernel["HalfPLRA"]. HalfPLRA is not free: Solution.py:2279 derives it as bool(HalfPLR & 0x01) from the int param HalfPLR. Bit-AND with 0x01 modeled in z3 as (HalfPLR % 2 == 1). True iff HalfPLR is odd.

grid_enumeration.domain: HalfPLR in {0,1,2,3}; HalfPLRA derived = bool(HalfPLR & 0x01) (4 cells)

crosshair.caveat: Absence of a counterexample from CrossHair is NOT a proof of correctness; it is bounded symbolic exploration over int.

verification.method: Evaluated bool(v & 0x01) for v in 0..3 in-container; truth table {0:F,1:T,2:F,3:T} matches z3 model and grid exactly.

classification_rationale: Predicate kernel["HalfPLRA"] is a truthiness test on a Solution dict entry that is a pure compile-time-derived boolean: HalfPLRA = bool(HalfPLR & 0x01), a bitwise AND of an integer solution parameter with a constant. No isinstance on live objects, no nodeType dispatch over a parsed tree, no os/filesystem/gpu probe participates in the predicate. The value is fully determined by the integer config param HalfPLR. Hence fully-static. solver_status is sat-bounded because HalfPLR was bounded to the seeded domain {0,1,2,3}; the relation generalizes to any int (true iff low bit set).
